description: Version 3.3, gripper plus handles plus base (builds on 3.2, related: voice-e3cd53d6; 3.1 is voice-5b59d3bf): Reduce the handle height again: just barely taller than the gripper fingers themselves. Rework how the handle attaches to the base and gear system so it attaches much more smoothly. Put the gears in the same plane as the gripper fingers (move the gears up), with a single motor centered there. The handle wraps around and connects into the gear system. Iterate on every piece as needed for this layout. Keep it parameterized (params.json and the Tune sliders), keep the pieces separable, and keep it driven by the single RobStride RS00.

results.identified_issue:
Folder Two Finger Gripper/versions/v303_generalist_inplane (copied from v302, params-first). Key decisions and why:
1) 'Height' = slide_h, the plate's extent across the finger's thickness (Y); 3.2 shrank the same dimension (37->29). New param handle_over; slide_h = plate + 2*handle_over = 15. slot_gap removed. Strap slots can't flank a 12 mm finger in 15 mm, so they became a y-through tunnel in a boss on the outer face (strap_slot_width = tunnel gap 2.5, slot_wall = boss wall 1.5). stop_width cut 2->1 to fit (assert). Genus: handle 1 hole.
2) Centred single motor + counter-rotating fingers: a pinion meshing both side gears gives co-rotation (wrong), so the pinion (on x=0, below the pivots at pin_theta=60 deg for 34 teeth) meshes only the right gear; right meshes left on the centreline as in 3.1/3.2. Left gear's tooth span is limited (teeth_span(), gear_extra) so its teeth stay clear of the pinion over 0-30 deg (check pinion_never_touches_the_left_side). Rejected: worm drive (symmetric and also centred, but non-backdrivable, which loses RS00 QDD current sensing, and is hard to model and check); idler chain (asymmetric, more parts); internal ring gear. Pinion phase = pin_theta + (frac(pin_theta/pitch) - 0.5)*pinion pitch; positive control (pinion half a tooth off interferes) passes.
3) In-plane gears: the finger's pivot is INSIDE the finger's base corner (J-hook), so an in-plane gear can't have a hub at its axis. Each gear = teeth (y +-gear_w/2) + a solid fan/hub below the finger, cut by offset(fit) handle2d and offset(tail_gap+fit) profile above web_y1 (the cradle), + a web at y < -slide_h/2-fit reaching the axis, + an axle into a plain base bushing. The cut uses tail_gap+fit round the finger because offset(fit) of both finger and tail left a zero-thickness sliver (non-manifold).
4) Tail = band between offset(tail_gap) and offset(tail_gap+slide_t) of the finger profile, windowed in rail (w,u) coords (u <= tail_top_u, w >= -tail_reach). The band is nearly concentric with the pivot, so on its own it only drove the handle open (closing had ~4 deg of play: the controls failed at -3 deg). Added a radial key (key_deg -90, straight down from the pivot) whose sides face tangentially, so it drives both ways with ~1.5 deg of play from the 0.2 fit. Checks: rotating the gear +-2 deg hits the handle.
5) Exports switched to the Manifold backend (export_models.py), with face-coincidence fixes (the boss starts mid-plate so its rounding stays inside; side-gear teeth slab has no root circle, the fan supplies it).
Not verified: no print or load test; the unit isn't retained in +y; no swing stops; the gallery hinge for 'Pinion' doesn't turn it (only ^Right/^Left swing), same as the motor. check_gripper_closure.py 'never touches' fails identically on all of 1.20-3.3, as it already did before this change.
results.summary: Made gripper 3.3: the handle is now 15 mm tall, it wraps around the base hook into a keyed cradle in its gear, and the gears sit in the finger plane, driven by one centred RS00 through a pinion.
results.detailed_description:
Handle: it is now 15 mm across the finger (was 29; the finger is 12). That leaves no room for strap slots beside the finger, so the strap runs through a tunnel under a raised boss on the plate's outer face (where your finger rests): in one face, out the other, around your digit. Its tail is a band that follows the finger's outline over the base hook, around it and under the finger, with a key sticking straight down.

Drive: the gears are now in the fingers' plane, just below the fingers. Each gear's hub is a cradle shaped to the finger and tail, with a notch for the key, so the finger and handle drop straight in and the gear drives them both ways. The RS00 sits on the centreline. Its pinion (1:1) meshes only the right gear, and the right gear meshes the left. A pinion meshing both gears would turn them the same way, so the fingers couldn't close. The left gear has teeth only where it needs them, so it never reaches the pinion. All 33 geometry checks pass. Everything stays in params.json and the Tune panel, with 7 new sliders, e.g. handle_over, pinion_teeth and key_r.

Tradeoffs: the boss sits your digit 4 mm further out over a 24 mm length. The unit sits in its cradle by fit and gravity, and nothing stops it lifting out. The left gear only has teeth for 0–30°. Nothing is printed yet. Check the Tune panel's Base picker for 3.3.

summary: Gripper version 3.3 needs handles barely taller than the fingers, attached more smoothly to a base and gear system moved up into the fingers' plane. Gears should surround one centered motor, with the handle wrapping into them, all parameterized, separable, and driven by the RobStride RS00.
